title: For Chinese Equities, The Good News Is In Short Supply
text:
For Chinese Equities, The Good News Is In Short Supply

Thomas Gatley

Gavekal Dragonomics | 9 Nov 2026

It’s been a bumpy week in a bumpy year for Chinese equity markets. Market regulators, the People’s Bank of China and the National Team all stepped into the breach after the benchmark CSI 300 fell 8.5% in October, its worst month in more than a decade, but the onshore market is still down 14% for the year. Fundamentally, China’s market fortunes are tied squarely to global sentiment on the artificial-intelligence boom, and particularly about the pace of the US data center buildout. This reliance on a single story is particularly intense in the absence of any significant improvement in weak domestic demand. While China’s policymakers continue to struggle to boost sustainable demand, however, the supply of newly tradeable stocks hitting the market should continue to shrink in 2027 to the lowest level in a decade. That creates a favorable foundation should sentiment rebound.
